sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: PrivateGPT is an open-source API layer for building private AI applications on top of models you run yourself. It adds messages, document ingestion, retrieval with citations, tools and MCP connectors on top of any OpenAI-compatible model server, and follows the Claude API design.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running a local model is only the first step; useful apps also need document search, tools and a stable API. PrivateGPT provides those building blocks so you can build private AI products without sending data to a cloud provider.
whoFor: Developers building private, on-premise AI apps
Teams that need RAG with citations on their own documents
Organisations with data that can't leave their servers
Claude Code or Claude Desktop users who want local models behind them
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when you already run a model server like Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp and need an application API on top. It doesn't run models itself.
requirements: A running OpenAI-compatible model server (Ollama is the easiest start)
Python 3.11 via uv on Linux and Windows, or Homebrew on macOS
Enough memory for your model (the README's Qwen example is about 24 GB)

overview: PrivateGPT sits between your app and an inference server. It connects to any server that implements /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models through the OPENAI_API_BASE setting, and exposes its own API at http://localhost:8080 that follows the Anthropic API spec.

It provides a standard messages API with streaming and token counting, file ingestion, retrieval with citations and agentic RAG, built-in tools mirroring the Claude API (web search, web fetch, code execution), custom tools, MCP connectors, and structured access to databases and CSVs.

A built-in workbench UI at /ui lets you send messages, upload documents, test retrieval and configure tools, but the API is the product. Integration guides cover Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cowork, Claude for Microsoft 365, and OpenCode. PrivateGPT is maintained by Zylon, which sells an enterprise platform built on it.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from PrivateGPT's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Install
steps.code:
brew tap zylon-ai/tap
brew install private-gpt

environment.name: OPENAI_API_BASE
environment.description: URL of your OpenAI-compatible model server, ending in /v1.

environment.name: OPENAI_EMBEDDING_API_BASE
environment.description: URL of the server that provides embeddings, ending in /v1.

tutorial.title: Chat with your documents using Ollama and PrivateGPT
tutorial.useCase: Run a local model with Ollama and use PrivateGPT's workbench to upload documents and ask questions.

steps.title: Pull the models and start Ollama
steps.body: The README's example LLM is about 24 GB and the embedding model about 670 MB.
steps.code:
ollama pull qwen3.5:35b
ollama pull mxbai-embed-large
ollama serve

steps.title: Start PrivateGPT
steps.body: Replace the ports with your Ollama server's port.

steps.title: Open http://localhost:8080/ui
steps.body: Pick a model, upload a document and ask a question to test retrieval with citations.

tutorial.expected: The workbench lists your models, ingests your documents and answers with citations. The API is available at http://localhost:8080.
